title: VR AI Game dev - Lessons from modding
author: Reklaw12
selftext:
I'm coming out of a couple weeks trying to wedge VR support into Space Marine 2 and I'd love to get some feedback on the lessons I think I learnt. I've been building Godot VR games with Claude for a while too but the different approach needed for an existing game was quite interesting to go through.

I have a writeup here [https://joe975.github.io/vr-modding-writeup/](https://joe975.github.io/vr-modding-writeup/) and some agent skills to hopefully help others skip the mistakes I made along the way [https://github.com/Joe975/vr-modding-with-agents](https://github.com/Joe975/vr-modding-with-agents)

Most of it came down to removing myself from the loop. Endless debugging performance issues, difference between eyes, or finicky to trigger motion controls drove me nuts until I remembered I should know better and just get the agents to do it all for me.

Once I had all that agent-testability & logging stuff down each playtest became an open mic session where I rambled about everything I didn't like while it logged my every move and game event, for later analysis and playback to validate fixes.

In my view we should be spending our time on the hard human-relevant bits:

* What feels boring/ok/GREAT as a player?
* Is the game fun to play?

Note this skips the HUGE effort of figuring out art for your game, so if you're looking for a break from that I highly recommend giving a mod a go!
